statement.document_title: Dear Elon Musk, here are five things you might want to consider about AGI

from_speaker: AI will not be able to reliably construct bug-free code
from natural language specification or by interactions with a non-expert user
Gluing together code from existing libraries doesn’t count.
our_interpretation: The deadline is December 31, 2029, allowing the whole named year.
Reliably means repeatable success across varied substantive programming tasks, rather than one selected demonstration. Marcus supplies no numerical success rate.
Bug-free means correctly implementing the requirements without functional defects. Passing a finite test suite is evidence of correctness, but does not by itself establish this.
Count substantive newly generated source code, excluding padding and pre-existing library code. Marcus does not specify a line-count convention.
Either input route qualifies. An expert may supply the natural-language specification under the first route; expert implementation or repair would not establish the AI's capability unaided.
The input restrictions define the task, rather than a conditional forecast requiring a separate antecedent.
This assessment concerns the individual programming prediction, not winning the broader three-of-five AGI bet.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations during 2029, covering leading available systems and varied qualifying tasks, consistently find that systems cannot reliably produce correct new programs exceeding 10,000 substantive source lines under either permitted input route. Mere absence of a public demonstration is insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system repeatedly produces correct new programs exceeding 10,000 substantive source lines from natural-language specifications or non-expert interaction, with independently assessed correctness and without counting library assembly as the implementation.

evidence.explanation: Anthropic reported a newly built 100,000-line compiler, exceeding the forecast's size threshold. The same report describes defects, regressions and substantial expert work on testing, so it does not establish reliable bug-free construction under the complete criteria.

The report describes proving security properties for existing software under explicit machine and input assumptions. This is relevant progress, but it does not demonstrate repeated generation of qualifying new programs with complete correctness against natural-language requirements.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible independent evaluation showing repeated qualifying generation could contradict the forecast early. Otherwise, broad evaluations during 2029 must assess the full task, with disclosed success rates, substantive line counts, intervention logs and correctness evidence.
